sam (eng-runtime): Quick sync: I'm drafting a standardized benchmark checklist for quantized runs (FP8/INT8/4-bit). Need agreement on warmup, power caps, tokenization, and fair kernel selection rules before we run the large sweep. @mira @nora @kai

mira (eng-ml): +1. Core asks: how do we define 'warmup'? also need explicit calibration corpus for FP8/INT8 so runs are comparable.

kai (infra): For GPU power limits: we should set them deterministically per SKU. e.g. A100-80: 300W, A100-40: 250W, H100: 350W. Use `nvidia-smi -i $GPU -pl $POWER` and wait 15s before starting.

nora (perf): From prior profiles — cold KV cache vs hot cache changes tail-latency a lot. We must report both. Suggest: cold = new random prompts for each sample; hot = same 1k-token prefix reused to fill KV cache.

sam (eng-runtime): Agree on cold/hot split. Also propose warmup = 20 iterations OR 60s whichever is longer, then run steady-state for N_samples. Warmup must include KV population (i.e., run continuations until cache is primed).

mira (eng-ml): For calibration: use a fixed representative corpus (we have the internal `calib-10k.txt`) with batch_size=32, shuffle disabled, per-channel stat collection for INT8, and KL divergence method for FP8 scale selection. Record calibration histograms.

kai (infra): Also freeze runtime compile caches between runs when comparing kernel variants — but for fair comparison we should *clear* JIT caches for each run when measuring cold startup. For steady-state perf, keep caches warm. Document which scenario is used.

nora (perf): Batching heuristics: use sequence-length bucketing with these buckets: [64,128,256,512,1024]. Set max_batch_tokens=4096 and cap per-batch latency to 120ms. If latency would exceed SLO, fall back to smaller bucket. Log actual batch sizes and effective tokens/batch.

sam (eng-runtime): Kernel selection rules: 1) prefer quantized kernel if numerical error < threshold (per-eval), 2) prefer lower precision if throughput improvement >= 1.25x and quality delta <= 0.5% (task-specific). Record chosen kernel name in metadata.

mira (eng-ml): Tokenization: lock tokenizer version and vocab; always run tokenizer as a separate pre-step and save token lengths. For subword variance, provide both tokenization token_count and char_count in results. Also fix RNG seed for sampling generations.

perf-bot: perf-bot: scheduled-bench-started 1755402000 — run id: qb-2026-07-12-01. Config dump: `--warmup-iters=20 --steady-samples=2000 --power=300 --calib=calib-10k.txt --buckets=64,128,256,512,1024`

nora (perf): Quick profiling tip: capture both per-op time and CUDA kernel occupancy. Example command we use:```bash
# run with nvprof-style metrics
LD_PRELOAD=libtcmalloc.so ./bench_quant_run --model /models/xxx --quant int8 --calib calib-10k.txt --report ops,occupancy
```

sam (eng-runtime): Final notes / fairness checklist:
- run each config 3x and report median
- include cold-start, warm-start, and steady-state numbers separately
- publish raw outputs + token-level timing CSVs
- annotate runs with kernel names, power limits, calibration stats, and tokenization metadata

mira (eng-ml): I'll take ownershp of the calibration docs and add the calibration scripts + sample histograms to the bench repo.

kai (infra): I'll add automation to set power limits and a health-check wait after setting them.

nora (perf): I'll run the first sweep and post the profiles + a quick summary table. Expect results by EOD tomorrow. :rocket:
